title: Henry McCullough rehearses with Wings | 1972
content:
In early 1972 Wings were preparing to go on the road, yet in rehearsals it became increasingly clear that they needed an additional guitarist.

Their initial line-up had Paul McCartney on and bass guitar, Linda McCartney on keyboards, Denny Laine on lead and rhythm guitar, and Denny Seiwell on drums. However, Linda’s musical ability was not enough to take the pressure off Laine, who was essentially fulfilling two roles.

Henry McCullough had been playing with Joe Cocker’s Grease Band until they split up in January 1972. Laine was friendly with McCullough and recommended him to McCartney. On 17 January Wings’ roadie Ian Horne was sent to invite McCullough to the band’s rehearsal the following day.

The rehearsal took place on 18 January 1972 at Scotch of St James, a nightclub and live music venue in central London.

I’d never met McCartney before. Once I got used to seeing him there in person, he turned out to be a great bloke. I guess I was a bit nervous, but I had a couple of pints of Guinness before I went along the first time. That helped.
Henry McCullough
New Musical Express, 29 January 1972

McCullough was invited to a second rehearsal on 20 January, after which he was invited to join Wings.
